tool: Search the corpus of Taiwanese snacks by attribute filters, keywords, or both; give at least one filter or keyword. An entry passes the filters when, for every field filtered on, it has at least one of the given values; an entry with no value in a field never passes a filter on that field. When keywords are given, an entry must also match at least one keyword in at least one of its English names. Returns at most ten matching entries, each with official name, aliases, English names, and attributes; more_results says whether there are more. An item sold in several versions is labeled by its most common version; when two versions are about equally common and the field allows more than one value, both are listed.

fields.dish_type: Dish type (required, one). Meal: a dish substantial enough and commonly eaten on its own as a meal, regardless of the time of day; it need not be nutritionally balanced. Snack: any other mainly savory food, side soups and side dishes included. Dessert: any other sweet food, pastries, sweet soups, and shaved ice included. Drink: drunk from a cup or through a straw, sweet or not, with or without add-ins.
fields.main_ingredients: Main ingredients (required, one to three). The ingredients a diner would name first. Noodles of any grain are Noodles, not Rice or Wheat; noodles are kneaded, cut, or extruded into strips, so batter scraped from the wok in pieces (ding bian cuo) is Rice. Wheat covers buns, dough, wrappers, and pastry. Starch is tapioca or sweet potato starch forming the body or defining texture of the dish (pearls, translucent wrappers, omelette batter, taro balls), not a thickener or a fried coating; taro, sweet potato, carrot, and daikon radish eaten as themselves are Root Vegetables. Soy covers soybeans, tofu, and soy milk. Beans and Seeds covers red beans, mung beans, peanuts, sesame, almonds, and aiyu seeds. Offal and blood go by their animal (pig's blood is Pork, duck blood is Poultry); Other Meat covers animals without their own value, such as lamb. Vegetables covers pickled and preserved vegetables (dried radish, pickled mustard greens). Fruit covers sugarcane. Sugar and Sweeteners covers brown sugar, maltose, honey, and syrups when the dish is named for that sweetener or tastes mainly of it; sugarcane itself stays Fruit. Tea covers tea leaves only; herbal and other "teas" go by their ingredient. Herbs covers grass jelly, herbal teas, Chinese medicinal herbs, mugwort, cudweed, roselle, and ginger.
fields.cooking_method: Cooking method (required, one or two). The step that gives the dish its character. Braised covers simmering and stewing in a soy-sauce-based liquid; a little soy sauce as seasoning does not count. Smoked covers smoking over sugar, tea, or wood, whether or not the food was cooked first. Dried covers sun-drying, air-drying, and oven-drying. Boiled covers boiling, poaching, blanching, and simmering or stewing in water, stock, or any other liquid that is not soy-sauce-based. Set means left to set into a curd or jelly. No Cooking means assembled from prepared parts (shaved ice, cut fruit, wraps and sandwiches). A drink the stall boils itself (herbal tea, winter melon tea, soy milk, rice milk) is Boiled; a drink pressed, blended, or assembled from prepared parts (sugarcane juice, papaya milk, boba tea) is No Cooking. A candy made from syrup the maker boils itself, alone or binding or coating nuts or fruit (maltose candy, peanut brittle, nougat, candied haws), is No Cooking.
fields.flavor: Flavor (required, one to three). Only tastes a first-time eater would notice. Bitter covers bitter melon, bitter herbal teas, and other plainly bitter foods. Spicy covers chili, pepper, and ginger heat. Fermented covers stinky tofu, century egg, and other foods with a pungent, fermented smell or taste.
fields.physical_form: Physical form (required, one). Dry: solid food served without broth, gravy, or substantial sauce; food with only a dipping sauce on the side is Dry. Sauced: food coated, tossed, or served with a substantial sauce, dressing, or seasoned oil, without being submerged in broth. Soup: pieces, curds, or jelly in a thin broth or syrup, eaten with a spoon. Thick Soup: a broth or sweet soup thickened with starch or flour. Shaved Ice: toppings on shaved or snow ice, eaten with a spoon. Ice Pop: frozen in one piece and eaten as is (on a stick, in a bag, or as a block). Smooth Drink: nothing to chew. Drink with Add-ins: pieces to chew (pearls, jelly, beans). Slush: blended ice, with or without add-ins. The three drink values are used exactly when Dish type is Drink.
fields.occasion: Occasion (optional, any number). An occasion is listed only when the association is culturally established and specific to the dish, not merely because the dish can be found there. Breakfast: commonly eaten for breakfast, or a staple of breakfast-shop menus. Night Market: a signature night-market stall item. Festival: traditionally associated with a specific festival, holiday, or culturally significant life-cycle ritual, even if the dish is also commonly eaten year-round. Souvenir: sold boxed as a regional gift.

keywords: Words or phrases matched against the entries' English names (common English translations and romanizations) as whole words or phrases, ignoring case and punctuation; a keyword also matches its plural, the keyword followed by s or es.

messages.rejected: The search was not run; the tool's schema rejects these arguments:
messages.no_filter_or_keyword: give at least one filter or keyword
messages.empty_keyword: has nothing but spaces and punctuation
